findings.title: Task and cluster verifiers fabricate completion
findings.evidence: pnpm task:verify T-G0-CORE and pnpm cluster:verify C-G0-IMPLEMENTATION exit 0 although no declared acceptance/negative test file, task result, independent review, lease, task commit, or cluster integration result exists. verifyTaskContract validates only generated contract metadata; cluster verification repeats that metadata check.

findings.title: Merge queue and lifecycle controls do not prove safe Git execution
findings.evidence: Task completion trusts --verified true; lifecycle omits IMPLEMENTING, SELF_REVIEWING, VERIFYING and MERGE_QUEUED; simulation hard-codes stale-lease/path-lock success; merge processing rebases the task branch in a way that can leave the cluster branch unadvanced; no real cluster result/review gate is consumed.

findings.title: Filesystem object store permits symlink escape and false immutable evidence hashes
findings.evidence: A controlled root/escape symlink allowed put('escape/payload') to write outside the configured root. Re-putting different bytes at an existing key swallowed EEXIST and returned the new-byte hash while the old bytes remained persisted.

findings.title: PostgreSQL transaction and readiness semantics are incorrect
findings.evidence: A live transaction callback insert survived an injected rollback because work(this) uses the pool instead of the transaction-scoped Sql. /readiness returned 200 ready against a live but empty database with zero application tables; partial or missing migration state is invisible.

findings.title: Mutation, placeholder and prohibited-capability scans are bypassable
findings.evidence: A controlled executable broadcastSignedPayload implementation passed prohibited-capabilities:scan. A controlled it.skip test passed placeholders:scan and pnpm test exited 0 with one skipped test. Scans cover only apps/packages and use narrow lexical patterns.

findings.title: Generated task contracts are not executable or correctly scoped
findings.evidence: All 70 contracts allow infra/migrations/** although only four have migration budget; representative write sets include paths outside allowed paths; read sets point to nonexistent schema files; 44 declared owner paths do not yet exist; verificationCommands recursively invoke task:verify; 184 acceptance IDs are assigned to multiple tasks without evidence ownership.

findings.title: Dashboard does not obtain readiness data through the API
findings.evidence: The SvelteKit load function returns a static generatedAt and static section list; it never calls PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL or an API route. The browser test proves only disclaimer text.

findings.title: Configured S3 object storage is ignored and local stack lacks bucket provisioning
findings.evidence: Config accepts OBJECT_STORE_DRIVER=s3 but does not parse S3 settings, while API main always constructs FilesystemObjectStore and labels it with the configured driver. MinIO required manual alias/bucket creation before the S3 adapter smoke passed.

findings.title: Production configuration fails open to development defaults
findings.evidence: loadConfig({NODE_ENV:'production'}) accepts default local database credentials, filesystem storage and default origin; required production fields are not conditionally enforced.

findings.title: Fake adapters can report generic AVAILABLE state
findings.evidence: ShadowNotificationAdapter and multiple Fake* adapters return status AVAILABLE without a typed synthetic/non-production capability marker. Naming or delivery-id prefixes are not an enforceable capability contract.

findings.title: Walking skeleton and deterministic simulation coverage are incomplete
findings.evidence: The sole walking-skeleton test uses pg-mem and an in-memory object store. It does not prove live PostgreSQL/MinIO integration, historical as-of replay selection, workflow crash/resume, lost lease, quota reset, model unavailability, notification terminal failure, or late-observation replay. Trace continuity is not persisted and artifact byte metadata is hard-coded to 1.

findings.title: Compiler lacks the required frozen semantic-stage artifact and complete drift closure
findings.evidence: Two generations are byte-identical, but no versioned content-addressed semantic artifact exists. Drift checking compares expected files only and does not reject unexpected files under generated roots. Generated integrity reports self-assert independent validation.

findings.title: CI does not exercise all claimed release gates
findings.evidence: CI lacks real task-result verification, cluster-result/review verification, worktree lifecycle, merge queue/revert execution, MinIO/S3 integration, API start/readiness smoke, compiler clean double-generation, and meaningful mutation checks for deleted/weakened/skipped tests.

findings.title: Bootstrap authority and release base are incomplete
findings.evidence: No bootstrap prompt was found in the repository or repository history. Neither local nor remote main exists. SSH authentication works, but GitHub API authentication and hosting controls cannot be inspected.

findings.title: MCP bootstrap transport lacks bounded resource controls
findings.evidence: The endpoint checks origin/content type/protocol but has no message-size, rate, concurrency or request-time bound. Missing Origin is accepted. These are explicit transport concerns even for a read-only synthetic bootstrap tool.

findings.title: Readiness and shutdown error handling are weak
findings.evidence: A rejected or hanging dependency check produces an unbounded Promise.all/500 path rather than a bounded not-ready result. Shutdown is not awaited by signal handlers before process lifecycle completion.

findings.title: Premature contracts and ineffective helpers reduce maintainability
findings.evidence: Provider contracts expose numerous future advanced-alpha interfaces without implementations; assertOutcomeLabelsDistinct is tautological for boolean inputs; the bootstrap contains abstractions not exercised by current runnable behavior.

externalControls.control: GitHub branch protection, required reviews, tag protection and repository rulesets
